scope: Proposition 5.2 (Dense truncation) of the manuscript “Routing densities and representation contraction for Thorp sweeps” (preprints/Routing-densities-and-representation-contraction-for-Thorp-sweeps-September-26-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 238 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4e5fbcff0dec65fd), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 20. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every ρ0 ∈ (0, 1] and ϵ > 0, there are c > 0 and n0 such that, for every dyadic n ≥ n0 and every integer r with ρ = r/n ∈ [ρ0, 1], the density exponent (5) exceeds r  H(ρ) + −ρ − (1 − ρ) ln(1 − ρ) ρ ln 2 + ϵ  with probability at most exp(−cr), uniformly in the input injection. The constants depend only on ρ0, ϵ, and the expression is interpreted continuously at ρ = 1.
